name: Conversational 30-Min Discovery Flow & Time Pacing Toolkit
description: Discovery calls feel like robotic BANT/MEDDIC interrogations and frequently run out of time before rep can uncover deep pain or secure committed next steps.
buyer: Account Executives and B2B Sales Reps
core_problem: Discovery calls feel like robotic BANT/MEDDIC interrogations and frequently run out of time before rep can uncover deep pain or secure committed next steps.
desired_outcome: Run fluid, 20-to-30-minute discovery calls that uncover high-value pain and lock in concrete next steps without making prospects feel grilled.
current_solutions: Rigid time-allocation frameworks (e.g., 2 mins intro, 18 mins discovery, 6 mins next steps)
Standardized discovery templates and cheat sheets
Qualification frameworks like BANT or MEDDIC
solution_gaps: Rigid time allocations break down when prospects digress.
Static qualification checklists force AEs into an interrogation dynamic instead of an organic business dialogue.
Existing cheat sheets don't provide transition phrases to bridge discovery into immediate next-step commitments.
basis: AEs repeatedly report running out of time and annoying prospects with interrogation-style qualification checklists on 30-minute discovery calls.
path: Conversational 30-Min Discovery Flow & Time Pacing Toolkit

problems.statement: Account Executives struggle to complete effective discovery within standard 30-minute call windows, running out of time before understanding deep buyer pain or setting next steps.
problems.normalized_problem: Insufficient call time to complete thorough discovery and establish next steps
problems.desired_outcome: Uncover critical business pain and align on clear next steps within a tight 30-minute timeframe without feeling rushed.
current_solutions: Rigid time-allocation frameworks (e.g., 2 mins intro, 18 mins discovery, 6 mins next steps)
Standardized discovery templates and cheat sheets
attempts: Allocating fixed minutes for rapport and agenda setting before asking discovery questions
solution_complaints: Light rapport and agenda setting consume half the call window, leaving minimal time to dive deep into buyer pain points.

problems.statement: Discovery calls often turn into dynamic interrogations or robotic question checklists, annoying buyers and stalling conversations.
problems.normalized_problem: Discovery calls feeling like interrogations rather than natural business conversations
problems.desired_outcome: Conduct fluid, engaging conversations that extract deep buyer insights without making prospects feel questioned or defensive.
current_solutions: Qualification frameworks like BANT or MEDDIC
attempts: Deploying tactical empathy techniques from sales books
Asking granular technical or infrastructure questions straight away
solution_complaints: Reps stall when prospects push back or answer outside the script
Deep technical questioning can make executive buyers combative or defensive

score.name: Conversational 30-Min Discovery Flow & Time Pacing Toolkit
